source.quote: Builds a governance-owned public-product manifest over the 39 done capabilities of CAPABILITIES.yaml: a four-axis truth model (implementationStatus / runtimeProof / availability / publicationStatus, kept deliberately separate), a fail-closed publication-ceiling policy, a real-git evidence verifier that admits no phantom commit/path/decision reference

Result: 0 public_marketable, 9 candidate, 30 internal_only, 3 blocked (prohibited_concept entries for Instagram self-serve publishing, Google Drive self-serve connect, and general creative-quality claims).

Amends derivePublicationCeiling so operator_only availability no longer categorically blocks public_marketable, matching ShortsOS V1's ratified managed/agency-operated go-to-market (request_pilot, never self-serve).

The gate now also clears when availability=operator_only AND the entity own claimCeiling carries no self-serve wording AND its prohibitedClaims already bans self-serve-style claims explicitly (managedServiceFramingHolds).

Human-ratified promotion (T0/Marc): M1-REAL-PRODUCE-REVIEW-PUBLISH moves from publicationStatus candidate to public_marketable, the sole entity of the nine SOS-PUBLIC-TRUTH-POLICY-V1 candidates whose own wording already clears the amended managed-service gate.
rejecting an earlier draft's stronger "runs your full pipeline for you" framing as overreaching the one-run evidence ceiling.

prohibitedClaims extended from 2 to 8 entries (the original 2 kept byte-identical) naming every forbidden implication: self-serve access, connecting your own Instagram account, publishing directly yourself, automatic publishing without review, universal availability, unproven repeated volume, guaranteed creative quality, guaranteed performance or virality.

two of them are one prohibitedClaims wording edit from also clearing the gate, but T0 explicitly ruled that is not sufficient reason to promote them now: they are provider-level implementation evidence, not necessary public product capabilities for V1.
when the codebase changes, does that change have a public-content consequence, and did anyone say so on purpose?
No record for a governed change is a hard failure, never a warning.
the only axis that is *derived*, never hand-set.
Any single failing condition caps the capability **below** `public_marketable` — never averaged toward it, never rounded up.
no amount of attached evidence is allowed to promote a concept the mandate names as never-claimable
